name: Salma
overview: Salma was a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Hur. He is noted for his connection to the founding of Bethlehem, an important city in biblical history. Beyond this, there are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Salma means 'little spark.' This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:51 and was not indicated as being given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Salma is explicitly identified as the son of Hur in Scripture, as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:51. No other family relationships beyond this are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Salma's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his lineage as the son of Hur and his association with the founding of Bethlehem. As a member of the tribe of Judah, his family line contributes to the heritage of this key city, which holds theological and historical importance in the Old Testament. His mention preserves the genealogical record that links the tribe of Judah to Bethlehem.
